title: Large rho tensor squares detect a nonzero invariant vector
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $S$ a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], with semisimple and simply connected defined as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, and use the character $\rho$, its extension $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$, and the actual regular-function modules $W_m\subseteq F[S]$ of [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with a coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying the coassociativity and counit identities; $V^S=\{v:\rho_V(v)=v\otimes1\}$. Tensor products have diagonal coaction. All equivariance and invariance below mean identities of coactions, equivalently identities after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. For every finite-dimensional rational $S$-module $V$ and every nonzero $v\in V^S$, there exists an integer $M\ge1$ such that for every integer $m\ge M$ there is an equivariant $F$-linear map
$$a_m:V\longrightarrow W_m\otimes_F W_m\quad\text{with}\quad a_m(v)\ne0.$$
The threshold may depend on $V$ and $v$; the assertion is for all sufficiently large $m$, not just for some unspecified subsequence.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), Seshadri Property I(b), p.247; Alper printed p.49. Apply to constant group S over R=F[[t]], V_R=V tensor R, and constant nonzero v; reduction gives the field map. Necessary nonvanishing hypothesis made explicit: the printed formulation cannot hold for v=0. Local PDF WANTED; HTML https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3#S9.SS7 read.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-double-flag-invariant-boundary], obtaining $Q,L,X,D,d,U,q$. In particular $X$ is integral, quasi-compact and separated, $U$ is dense and stable under $S$, $d$ is invariant, and $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=F[S]^{T,\mathrm{right}}$ equivariantly. We use this identification throughout.

source.place: Theorem 21.80, Example 21.83 and Theorem 21.84 (pp.450--451), Theorem 22.48 and Remark 22.49 (pp.479--480). Agent-formulated double-flag boundary consequence of the Bruhat and divisor descriptions; not quoted as a verbatim theorem of Milne.

proof.text: Construct a $T$-invariant functional $\lambda:V\to F$ with $\lambda(v)=1$ directly. Choose $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$; its coordinate ring has Laurent monomial basis $z^a$, $a\in\mathbf Z^r$. Write the restricted coaction as $\rho_T(u)=\sum_a p_a(u)\otimes z^a$. Coassociativity and linear independence of Laurent monomials give $\rho_T(p_a(u))=p_a(u)\otimes z^a$, and the counit gives $u=\sum_a p_a(u)$. Thus $p_0$ is a linear projection to the trivial weight space. Since $v$ is invariant, $p_0(v)=v$. Extend $v$ to a basis of this space and choose its coordinate functional $\lambda_0$ with $\lambda_0(v)=1$. Then $\lambda=\lambda_0p_0$ satisfies $\lambda(tu)=\lambda(u)$ as a coaction identity. This calculation uses characters, not their differentials, so also holds in positive characteristic.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, proof (a) implies (b), pp.234--235; coefficient calculation written out.

proof.text: For $u\in V$ define the regular matrix coefficient $c(u)(g)=\lambda(g^{-1}u)$. It is regular since the action, inversion and $\lambda$ are morphisms. The identity $c(u)(gt)=\lambda(t^{-1}g^{-1}u)=c(u)(g)$ shows that it is in $F[S]^{T,\mathrm{right}}$, hence defines $c:V\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ by Step 1. Moreover $c(su)(g)=\lambda(g^{-1}su)=c(u)(s^{-1}g)$, so $c$ is equivariant. These formulas hold at the universal points, hence are coaction identities. Finally $c(v)=1$ since $v$ is invariant and $\lambda(v)=1$.

source.place: Agent-written matrix-coefficient construction following the split-torus weight projection of Theorem 12.12.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology] with its scheme $X$, invertible sheaf $D$, section $d$, quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ and $p=0$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1; $\mathcal O_X$ is locally a free rank-one module. Every $c(e_i)$ for a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $V$ is therefore $b_i/d^{n_i}$ for some $n_i\ge0$ and $b_i\in\Gamma(X,D^{n_i})$. Put $N=\max(1,n_1,\ldots,n_{\dim V})$. For every $m\ge N$ define the linear map $b_m:V\to\Gamma(X,D^m)$ by $b_m(e_i)=d^{m-n_i}b_i$. On $U$ this gives $b_m(u)=d^m c(u)$. In particular it gives all integers $m\ge N$, with no congruence restriction.

source.place: Tag 09MR, lemma-invert-s-cohomology, p=0; common denominators on a finite basis.

proof.text: Restriction $\Gamma(X,D^m)\to\Gamma(U,D^m)$ is injective: on an affine trivializing open of the integral scheme $X$, a section is an element of a domain; if zero on its dense open intersection with $U$, it is zero. This also shows that the restriction is an injection of rational $S$-modules, since $U$ is stable. Tensoring this injection with $F[S]$ remains injective (choose and extend a basis over the field). On $U$, the identity $b_m=d^m c$, invariance of $d$ and equivariance of $c$ give the coaction identity for $b_m$; the tensor injection proves it on $X$. Thus $b_m$ is equivariant. Its value on $v$ restricts to $d^m$, which is nonzero on the nonempty $U$; consequently $b_m(v)\ne0$.

source.place: Agent-written uniqueness of section extension on an integral scheme and coaction verification.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] applied to the inverse character $-m\widetilde\rho$, $\Gamma(Q,L^m)=W_m$: the transformation formula is $f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^mf(g)$. Tensor powers have this character because the local transition functions multiply. Apply [lem-sc-external-global-sections-tensor-bijective] to $Q,Q,L^m,L^m$. The proper finite-type quotient $Q$ is quasi-compact and separated over $F$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], and $L^m$ is invertible, hence quasi-coherent. Its map gives an isomorphism $\theta_m:W_m\otimes_F W_m\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,D^m)$. This map is equivariant: on a pure tensor it pulls back the two sections and multiplies them, operations commuting with translation; linearity gives the coaction identity. Set $a_m=\theta_m^{-1}b_m$. It is equivariant, and $a_m(v)\ne0$ since $b_m(v)\ne0$. With $M=N$, this proves the stated conclusion for every $m\ge M$.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, degree zero; homogeneous section convention from Milne Theorem 22.48.
